title: fix(plugin-security)!: split controlled_by_parent write refusals by true semantics
body:
Fixes #7474

`assertControlledByParentWrite` funnelled **six** distinct conditions through one `deny()` helper, so all six answered `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` with one sentence — "requires edit access to its master record". Three of them are genuine authorization verdicts. The other three are not verdicts at all, and the shared sentence was a false statement carrying a false remedy: "ask whoever owns the parent record" cannot fix a null master FK, a deleted row, or an object that declares `controlled_by_parent` with no `master_detail` relation to derive access from.

## The ruling this implements

Maintainer ruling of 2026-08-11, recorded on #7474 and quoted verbatim:

> Ruling: **split the six legs by true semantics.** The three genuine authorization legs (no object-level update / write-RLS / no share grant) keep `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` with the current sentence. The three non-verdict legs change: `controlled_by_parent declared but no master_detail relation` → a loud configuration-defect error (it is a precisely detectable authoring defect, not an access verdict); `target record not found` → 404; `detail record has no master reference` → 422 validation-shaped. Envelope vocabulary per ADR-0112; coordinate with #7450 (ruled in the same session).

## What the six legs answer now

| condition | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| no object-level `update` on the master | `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` | unchanged, sentence verbatim |
| master row outside the caller's write RLS | `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` | unchanged, sentence verbatim |
| no `edit`-level share grant on the master | `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` | unchanged, sentence verbatim |
| `controlled_by_parent` with no `master_detail` relation | `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` | **`422 INVALID_METADATA`** |
| the target detail row does not exist | `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` | **`404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND`** |
| the detail's master reference is empty | `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` | **`422 MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD`** |

**No new error code.** All three are drawn from the existing ADR-0112 vocabulary, per the ledger's own guidance that a generic condition takes an existing entry rather than a registered synonym. `packages/spec` is untouched — see "Out of scope" for the one provenance row that belongs to the spec seat.

## Three decisions worth reviewing

**Why the new messages do not open with `[Security] Access denied`.** That exact prefix is a **matcher**, not a house style: `isPermissionDeniedError`, `mapDataError` and `rest-server`'s sanitiser all read it as "this is a 403". A configuration defect phrased with that opening would be re-flattened to `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` at the transport and the split would be invisible on the wire. Each class opens with a prefix of its own, and the tests assert the absence.

**Why the explanation lives in `message` and never in `details`.** Per #7450 (ruled the same session, cli lane) `details` is off the dispatcher wire, and `mapDataError`'s 4xx passthrough keeps only `error`, `code` and `object`. So nothing here is designed to depend on `details` reaching a client — each message stands alone, names the object, the operation and the remedy, and is written for the app author.

**Why 422 and not 500 for the metadata defect.** A 500 would be the "server fault" reading, but both transports drop a 5xx producer's prose unconditionally — and prose *is* the entire remedy for this condition. `422 INVALID_METADATA` is also the shape `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` already uses for "your metadata is broken", reused rather than spelled a second way. The two 422 legs stay distinguishable by `code`, which is the field ADR-0112 makes the branch point.

Each error carries both `status` and `statusCode`: `mapDataError` passes a domain error through on `.status` alone, while the dispatcher's `errorFromThrown` reads `.status` then falls back to `.statusCode`.

## The 404 is not an oracle — verified, not assumed

The dispatch asked this to be measured rather than presumed, and it holds in both halves:

- The detail row is probed under a **system** context (`readRowById(…, { isSystem: true })`, short-circuited at `security-plugin.ts` step "`opCtx.context?.isSystem`"), so a row hidden from the caller by read RLS is still **found** here and falls through to the authorization legs.
- The object-level CRUD gate (middleware step 2) and the row-level write pre-image check (step 2.7) both run **before** this gate, so a caller who reaches it already holds `update` on the detail.

Both halves are pinned by a test that asserts the RLS-hidden row still answers `403`, next to the one asserting the absent row answers `404` — that pairing is what makes "404" mean "absent".

One honest residual, filed rather than widened into this PR: `readRowById` swallows engine exceptions into the same `null`, so a driver outage reaches the not-found leg too and now answers 404 (it answered 403 before). Filed as #7505.

## Tests

Nine new cases in `controlled-by-parent-sharing.test.ts`, on the same fixture the suite has always used. Each asserts the ADR-0112 pair (`code` **and** `status`) — the defect here is the envelope, not the refusal, so a `rejects.toThrow()` would stay green on precisely the reported behaviour. The three authorization legs additionally assert their sentence verbatim, because on those legs the wording is the contract.

Two legs had no coverage at all before this (no object-level `update` on the master; master row outside the write RLS) — both now boot a permission set shaped for them.

**Reverse verification** — the fix was taken out with `git checkout origin/main --` on the two source files (never `git stash`), and the direction was predicted before running: 5 red expected — the three new-envelope cases, the insert variant, and the distinguishability case — with the three `403` cases and the RLS-hidden case staying green. Measured exactly that: `Tests 5 failed | 22 passed (27)`, each failure being `PERMISSION_DENIED` received where the new code was expected. Restored, `27 passed`.

**Consumer sweep.** Grep for the six leg fragments repo-wide found exactly one consumer pin outside the edited file (`/requires edit access to its master/`, an authorization leg — kept verbatim). Grep is necessary and not sufficient here, so the consumer suites were run: `@objectstack/dogfood` 546 passed (includes `showcase-invoice-cbp.dogfood.test.ts`), `@objectstack/example-crm` 27, `@objectstack/example-showcase` 168, `@objectstack/runtime` 1939, `@objectstack/rest` 1341, `@objectstack/plugin-security` 931 (full suite). Gates: `check:nul-bytes`, `check:error-code-casing`, `check:docs-audit-scope` green; `typecheck` clean.

## Out of scope, filed

- **#7503** — publish-time lint for `controlled_by_parent` with no `master_detail`. Question 2 of the card, which the ruling deliberately did not order. Confirmed statically detectable: the rule family already lives in `packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts` and the relation resolution is the same three-step fallback `resolveCbpRelation` performs.
- **#7504** — ledger provenance: `INVALID_METADATA` now has a second emitter and is registered under one. No wire or gate consequence today (the union dedupes); it is the retirement rule that reads those rows as the emitter list. One line, in the spec seat's file.
- **#7505** — `readRowById` collapses "absent", "engine threw" and "no engine" into one `null`.

`packages/runtime` and `packages/rest` are untouched — that surface is #7450's.
